import mir_eval
import numpy as np

# Define a deterministic 2-layer hierarchy for both reference and estimation
ref_intervals_hier = [
    np.array([[0.0, 30.0]]),
    np.array([[0.0, 15.0], [15.0, 30.0]])
]
ref_labels_hier = [["A"], ["a", "b"]]

est_intervals_hier = [
    np.array([[0.0, 30.0]]),
    np.array([[0.0, 15.0], [15.0, 30.0]])
]
est_labels_hier = [["A"], ["a", "b"]]

# Compute L-measure scores
l_precision, l_recall, l_measure_val = mir_eval.hierarchy.lmeasure(
    ref_intervals_hier, 
    ref_labels_hier, 
    est_intervals_hier, 
    est_labels_hier, 
    frame_size=0.1
)

# Verify that identical hierarchies yield perfect scores
assert np.isclose(l_precision, 1.0), f"Expected precision 1.0, got {l_precision}"
assert np.isclose(l_recall, 1.0), f"Expected recall 1.0, got {l_recall}"
assert np.isclose(l_measure_val, 1.0), f"Expected f-measure 1.0, got {l_measure_val}"

print(f"__CHECK__ lmeasure {l_precision:.1f}, {l_recall:.1f}, {l_measure_val:.1f}")
